question: _______ is a famous Kathak dancer.  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Josyula Seetharamaiah
Padma Subrahmanyam
Birju Maharaj
Geeta Chandran
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Birju Maharaj

Explanation:
Birju Maharaj is one of the most famous Kathak dancers in India. He represents the Lucknow Gharana and has given global recognition to Kathak dance. Born on 4 February 1938, he has been honored with the Padma Vibhushan, Padma Shri, and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. Other options: Josyula Seetharamaiah was a Telugu scholar, Padma Subrahmanyam is a Bharatanatyam dancer, and Geeta Chandran is also known for Bharatanatyam. Hence, in the context of Kathak dance, Birju Maharaj is the correct answer.

question: Which is the most traded-around currency of the world? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: INR
Dinar
USD
Euro
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is USD

Explanation:
The most traded currency in the world is the US Dollar (USD). It is involved in about 88% of all foreign exchange transactions globally, making it the world's primary reserve currency. The dominance of USD is due to the stability of the US economy, its widespread use in global trade, and its central role in the international financial system. Many countries peg their currencies to the USD, and it is primarily used in international trade. The Euro is the second most traded currency, while INR and Dinar have a very small share in global trade.

question: According to the United Nations which year is considered as the International Year of Indigenous Languages? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (17/02/2021) Shift 1)

question: The 'Bretton Woods Twins' refers to the two multilateral organisations created at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944. They are ______ and ______. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: IMF, World Bank
UN, World Bank
IMF, WTO
IMF, UN
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is IMF, World Bank

Explanation:
The Bretton Woods Conference in 1944 established the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank, collectively known as the 'Bretton Woods Twins'. The IMF aims to promote global monetary cooperation and provide assistance to countries facing balance of payments crises. The World Bank provides long-term loans and technical assistance for economic development in developing countries. WTO was established in 1995, and the United Nations was founded in 1945, so these are not products of the Bretton Woods Conference. Thus, the correct pair is IMF and World Bank.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Where is the IMF headquarters located? → Washington D.C.
☛ What was the original name of the World Bank? → International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)
☛ When did the Bretton Woods system end? → 1971
☛ In which year was the WTO established? → 1995

Solution: सही उत्तर है IMF, विश्व बैंक

Explanation:
1944 में ब्रेटन वुड्स सम्मेलन में अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मुद्रा कोष (IMF) और विश्व बैंक की स्थापना की गई थी। इन दोनों संगठनों को सामूहिक रूप से 'ब्रेटन वुड्स ट्विन्स' कहा जाता है। IMF का उद्देश्य वैश्विक मौद्रिक सहयोग को बढ़ावा देना और भुगतान संतुलन संकटों में देशों को सहायता प्रदान करना है। विश्व बैंक का उद्देश्य विकासशील देशों में आर्थिक विकास के लिए दीर्घकालिक ऋण और तकनीकी सहायता प्रदान करना है। WTO (विश्व व्यापार संगठन) 1995 में स्थापित हुआ, जबकि संयुक्त राष्ट्र 1945 में बना था, अतः ये ब्रेटन वुड्स सम्मेलन के उत्पाद नहीं हैं। अतः सही युग्म IMF और विश्व बैंक है।

IBM का पूर्ण रूप International Business Machines है। IBM Corporation एक अमेरिकी बहुराष्ट्रीय प्रौद्योगिकी कंपनी है जिसका मुख्यालय न्यूयॉर्क में है। इसकी स्थापना 1911 में हुई थी और यह कंप्यूटर हार्डवेयर, सॉफ्टवेयर और क्लाउड कंप्यूटिंग सेवाओं के लिए जानी जाती है। IBM ने पर्सनल कंप्यूटर (PC) के विकास में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई है। कंपनी का नाम मूल रूप से Computing Tabulating Recording Company था, जिसे 1924 में बदलकर International Business Machines कर दिया गया।

question: When did the British enact the Inland Emigration Act?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: 1861
1859
1857
1856
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1859

Explanation:
The British government enacted the Inland Emigration Act in 1859 to regulate the movement of laborers in India. This act aimed to control the recruitment and transportation of workers for plantations and mines. Under this act, laborers were required to work under contracts, and their movement was restricted. It primarily applied to workers in tea, coffee, and indigo plantations. The act facilitated the exploitation of laborers by binding them to specific employers and locations. It was a key piece of legislation during the British colonial period to manage labor supply for commercial agriculture.

question: In which conference were The World Bank and its sister institution the International Monetary Fund created by the United Nations?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/03/2021) Shift 1)
options: Atlantic Conference
U. N. Conference on Trade and Employment
International Conference on Financing for Development
Bretton Woods Conference
solution:
Solution: Correct answer is Bretton Woods Conference

Explanation:
After World War II, a conference was held in July 1944 at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, USA, to rebuild the global economy. Delegates from 44 countries participated. The conference led to the creation of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), which later became part of the World Bank Group. Both institutions are specialized agencies of the United Nations. The Bretton Woods system established fixed exchange rates and promoted international financial cooperation.

question: Long Radio waves were discovered by (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Guglielmo Marconi
W. Rontgen
Issac Newton
Heinrich Hertz
solution:

While Heinrich Hertz experimentally proved the existence of radio waves, Marconi is credited with their practical application and long-distance transmission.

question: The parliament of Norway is called: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: The National Diet
Folketing
Parliament
Stortinget
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Stortinget

Explanation:
The parliament of Norway is called the Stortinget, which means "the Great Assembly". It is the supreme legislative body of Norway and was established in 1814. Stortinget is a unicameral parliament with 169 members elected for four-year terms. In contrast, the National Diet is the parliament of Japan, the Folketing is the parliament of Denmark, and Parliament is a general term used for legislative bodies in many countries. Hence, the correct answer is Stortinget.
